title: The Last Choir Again
premise: Mara Lockridge has survived eight years as the crown's food-taster by learning which poisons kill slowly and which loyalties die faster. When a dying courier presses a map of the Thornfell smuggler roads into her hands along with a shard of dragon-scale, she becomes the unwilling bearer of an old covenant between the mountain clans and the last dragon, Emberwake, whose fading fire holds the realms' fragile peace together. Hunted by the king's spymaster—who wants the covenant broken so the crown can seize the dragon's hoard—and shadowed by the stranger's vengeful daughter, Mara must cross every forbidden road she knows to reach Emberwake's hollow before the fire gutters out. In the end she reforges the covenant not with royal ink but by offering her own poisoned blood as witness, toppling the spymaster through clan justice rather than law, and choosing exile among the mountains over a throne's gratitude.
about_author: Edmund Winterbourne is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy obsessed with borders—geographic, moral, and mortal—from a farmhouse whose cellar allegedly connects to no smuggler's road whatsoever.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Mara. At the royal court, Mara detects henbane in the king's wine but realizes the poison was meant for her—the spymaster knows what the dying courier carried. That night she finds the courier bleeding out in the tasters' quarters; he presses a scale-shard map into her hands and names Emberwake. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into reluctant resolve as survival demands she run.

chapters.title: Roads She Swore She'd Forgotten
chapters.summary: POV Mara, with interludes from Sera, the courier's daughter tracking her. Fleeing into Thornfell, Mara uses half-remembered smuggler roads while evading the spymaster's riders, and barges past clan wards that test her blood and find old covenant marks in it. Sera catches up intending vengeance but instead shares proof her father was clan-born. Emotional beat: bitter trust kindling between enemies.

chapters.title: What the Fire Asks
chapters.summary: POV alternates Mara and the spymaster, Corvane. Reaching Emberwake's guttering hollow, Mara learns the covenant requires a willing witness marked by poison survived—but Corvane arrives with the king's seal and an offer: betray the dragon, gain wealth and pardon. The clans turn on each other as his gold spreads corruption. Emotional beat: temptation at its peak, power's price made flesh.

chapters.title: The Last Choir
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Refusing Corvane, Mara drinks the covenant draught laced with every poison she has ever tasted, letting her scarred blood bind the renewed oath as Emberwake's fire roars back and burns Corvane's claim to ash. Clan justice—not royal law—sentences his surviving agents. Mara declines a place at court, staying as the dragon's sworn warden. Emotional beat: costly peace, chosen exile, quiet triumph.
